text:
MPC fell 0.9% today and has dropped 9% over the past two weeks, tracking a broader unwinding of the refinery boom that powered energy stocks through much of the year. The timing coincides with news that the "money-making energy trade looks over"—a shift driven by moderating oil prices (US crude at $89.53, down from earlier highs), refineries already running at 95.7% capacity with ample fuel in storage, and expectations that the exceptional margins refiners enjoyed are fading as supply-demand dynamics normalize.

Geopolitical tension in the Middle East—including Iranian drone and missile attacks on Saudi and Bahrain facilities, tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi claims against refineries—has not been enough to offset the fundamental shift in refinery economics. With gasoline and diesel inventories elevated and the broader market consensus turning away from energy as a standalone profitable trade, the stock has entered a downtrend that reflects profit-taking after the sector's earlier run.
